set_aside.subject: lazy creation of the manual budget during progress listing
set_aside.text: “project_tracking.list_project_progress … first creates the empty manual budget version” conflicts with State 3: “budget_management owns … the manual budget” and project_tracking “Must not own … budget editing.”
set_aside.question: Which module and capability own the creation triggered by list_project_progress: project_tracking itself or budget_management.ensure_manual_budget?
options: a new coordinating capability owns the combined operation
set_aside.default_guess: Have list_project_progress delegate creation to budget_management.ensure_manual_budget.

witness.initial: An archived project has no manual BudgetVersion, and an authorized staff member may read its progress.
events: The staff member requests the progress list.
A module-boundary test observes calls and repository access while list_project_progress creates the required empty version.
outcomes: The test observes project_tracking calling budget_management.ensure_manual_budget.
The test observes project_tracking writing the budget through persistence itself, despite budget_management owning manual budgets.
witness.observer: The module-boundary implementer or focused ownership test

set_aside.subject: transaction boundary of progress-list budget creation
set_aside.text: “the progress list first creates the empty manual budget version …” does not say whether that creation and its required budget.manual_version_create audit commit separately from, or atomically with, reading and returning the progress list.
set_aside.question: If creating the empty budget succeeds but the subsequent progress read fails, must the budget version and audit remain committed or be rolled back?
options: Commit creation and audit first, then perform the progress read in a separate read transaction
Create, audit and read in one transaction that rolls back together on failure
set_aside.default_guess: Create and audit in one write transaction with the progress read, committing only when the whole list operation succeeds.

witness.initial: An archived project has no manual BudgetVersion and its progress repository will fail when read.
events: Authorized staff requests the progress list.
The empty manual budget and its audit are prepared.
The progress-record read raises a persistence failure.
outcomes: The request fails, but the empty budget version and budget.manual_version_create audit remain committed.
The request fails and both the empty budget version and audit are rolled back.
witness.observer: The staff member on a later read, and an administrator inspecting budget or audit records

set_aside.unit: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
set_aside.subject: revocation observed by an already-authenticated request
set_aside.text: The changed text says “Immediate means every request authenticated after the revocation commits observes it,” while A11 and M07 say a revoked grant or assignment “blocks the next authorization check immediately.”
set_aside.question: If a request authenticates before revocation commits but performs its project authorization check afterward, must that check observe the revocation?
options: Yes; every authorization check after commit observes revocation, regardless of when authentication occurred
No guarantee applies to a request authenticated before commit; it may retain the old access decision
set_aside.default_guess: Require every authorization check begun after the revocation commit to observe it.

witness.initial: An operator has an active project assignment and a valid session.
events: The operator's request resolves its staff session into an actor context, then pauses before project authorization.
An administrator revokes the assignment and the revocation commits.
The operator's request resumes and performs its project authorization check.
outcomes: The next authorization check observes the revoked assignment and rejects the request.
Because the request authenticated before the commit, it may proceed using the pre-revocation access state.
witness.observer: The operator and anyone affected by the project read or mutation
